newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Mid-Apr diesel trades over $27.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Mid-Apr diesel trades over $27.

text.p: A flurry of diesel deals were done on Thursday for mid-April lifting cargoes at prices ranging between $27.15 and $27.85 per barrel, traders said.

They noted that even though these deals were more than $1.00 per barrel below the last deal done for early April at $28.60, it reflected the continuing firm diesel market which is now focused on the forward weeks in April.
But one trader noted that the market would not be able to sustain the high levels especially with the large volumes of arbitrage cargoes from Russia and the Middle East due to arrive to Asia soon.
Another trader said, "I don't think the level is sustainable."
They said physical prices should slip to around $26.50 per barrel fob, around the levels seen on the April swaps market, traders said.

Four diesel cargoes were traded on Thursday--a European major bought 220,000 barrels from a Chinese bunker trader at $27.25 for April 15-19, a Singapore trader bought 150,000 barrels from the same major at $27.50, a Japanese trader bought 190,000 barrels from a Malaysian trader at $27.85, and another 200,000-barrel cargo from a Western trader at $27.15 fob, basis.
Traders noted that with these purchases the Singapore trader added another 540,000 barrels to its more than three million barrels he bought over the last three weeks.

"He is a brave man to be able to buy at such high levels as far as the endusers are able to pay at such levels," one trader said. "If he failed to place those cargoes into Indonesia or China, he will find a hard time to place them elsewhere."

Other traders said that the European major has bought the 220,000 barrels from the Chinese bunker trader to cover its shorts into India. The major has sold seven diesel cargoes to India for April delivery.

Jet fuel was quiet with only one offer seen at $26.80 a barrel for April 15-19 lifting fob. While physical regrade remained to be at negative levels, swaps jet-gas oil regrade has widened slightly to 30/40 cents per barrel from Wednesday's 20-cent offer.
